diagnostic_evidence.quote: we consider the following self-adjoint eigenvalue problem: find $u \in H^2_0(\Omega)$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ such that
For impedance boundary conditions, we set $X \coloneqq H^2(\Omega)$

issues.failure_explanation: The eigenfunctions e^(i) solve a Dirichlet-type problem on H^2∩H^1_0, so they span only that subspace. For the hard and impedance cases X=H^2(Ω), and the expansion u=Σu^(i)e^(i) of an arbitrary u∈X is unjustified. Moreover A is not T-coercive on H^2(Ω) at all. For harmonic u_n (e.g. r^n cos nθ on a disk) normalised in H^2, a(u_n,v)=(∇u_n,∇v)-k^2(u_n,v), so ||A u_n||→0 and A is not bounded below. The form e(·,·) is not coercive on H^2(Ω). T-coercivity of A, and hence weak T-coercivity of 𝒜, is therefore unproven (and false for this A) for hard/impedance conditions.

failure_location.quote: Let $u \in X$ be arbitrary and $u^{(i)} \in \mathbb{C}$ s.t. $u = \sum_{i \in \mathbb{N}} u^{(i)} e^{(i)}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a T operator and eigenproblem adapted to the actual space and boundary conditions (e.g. a Neumann/Robin-type eigenproblem, or a different splitting into coercive part and compact part) must be constructed and shown to give T-coercivity or weak T-coercivity on H^2(Ω).
issues.overall_effect: Well-posedness for sound-hard and impedance conditions (β=0 and β>0), and the discrete T_h-coercivity built on the same construction for the impedance case, are unsupported. Only the sound-soft case, where X=H^2∩H^1_0, is covered.
issues.title: T built from Dirichlet eigenfunctions in H^2∩H^1_0 is used to claim T-coercivity of A on X=H^2(Ω) (hard/impedance)
issues.why_classification: The splitting A+K and the single T used for all three boundary conditions fail for X=H^2(Ω), so the hard and impedance analyses need a new construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we use the continuity of the normal trace operator and the compactness of the trace operator.
Since the trace operator $\gamma_0$ is compact, we have that $K u_n \to K u$ for any sequence $u_n \rightharpoonup u$ in $H^2$ and thus $K$ is compact.

issues.failure_explanation: For u∈H^2(Ω), Δu and n^T(Hu)n are only in L^2(Ω). Their traces on ∂Ω are not defined in L^2(∂Ω), and u↦γ0Δu is not bounded, let alone compact, from H^2 to L^2(∂Ω). Compactness of the trace operator applies to u, not to second derivatives. The bounds ||Ku|| ≤ C(||γ0Δu||+...) are therefore meaningless on X=H^2(Ω). The boundary terms (Δu,∇v·ν)_{∂Ω} in the sesquilinear forms are not even defined on that space.

failure_location.quote: Let $\gamma_0 : X \to L^2(\partial \Omega)$ denote the trace operator.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the boundary terms must be given a meaning (e.g. a higher-regularity solution space or a modified weak formulation) and compactness of K re-proved in that setting.
issues.overall_effect: Weak T-coercivity, and thus well-posedness, for sound-hard and impedance conditions (β=0 and β>0) is unsupported. The weak formulations (BFHard) and (BFImpedance) are ill-defined on H^2(Ω).
issues.title: Compactness of K relies on L^2(∂Ω) traces of Δu and of the Hessian, which do not exist for u in H^2
issues.why_classification: The functional framework for the hard/impedance cases has to be redesigned, not patched locally.

issues.failure_explanation: The λ^(i) are eigenvalues of the problem posed on H^2∩H^1_0 (sound-soft type). A nontrivial kernel element of the sound-hard operator lies in H^2(Ω) and satisfies Neumann-type conditions, so it is not an eigenfunction of that problem. The hypothesis k^2∉{λ^(i)} says nothing about it; injectivity requires k^2 to avoid the hard-BC spectrum, which is never assumed.

failure_location.quote: For sound hard boundary conditions this follows from the assumption that $k^2 \not \in \{ \lambda^{(i)} \}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and use the correct nonresonance hypothesis (k^2 not an eigenvalue of the corresponding sound-hard eigenproblem) and prove injectivity from it.
issues.overall_effect: The sound-hard case of Lemma Ainjective and the nonresonance condition for hard boundary conditions are unsupported; the same lemma for β>0 (lem:added-2) inherits the same gap in the hard case.
issues.title: Injectivity for sound-hard conditions deduced from the spectrum of the Dirichlet-type problem
issues.why_classification: The fix is a changed hypothesis plus a short argument. It is more than a typo because the stated nonresonance condition changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which implies that $\gamma_0 v = 0$ and $\gamma_0 \Delta v = 0$ on $\partial \Omega$
The rest of the proof follows analogously to the proof of \cref{lem:Ainjective}.

issues.failure_explanation: Young's inequality bounds a cross term from above. It cannot give a lower bound of |-αθ(Δv,v)+θ||v||^2| by a sum of squares, since the cross term has the opposite sign and the difference can vanish with Δv≠0, v≠0. The imaginary part of -α(Δv,∂_νv) is also ignored. The conclusion γ0v=γ0Δv=0, on which the unique-continuation argument rests, is therefore not established. In the fourth-order setting the boundary term is sign-indefinite, so the Helmholtz argument does not transfer.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a valid argument that a kernel element has vanishing boundary data (or a different uniqueness argument) must be supplied for the fourth-order impedance condition.
issues.overall_effect: Injectivity of 𝒜 for impedance boundary conditions (β=0 and β>0) is unproven, hence also well-posedness there and the discrete impedance analysis relying on Theorem vBZThm.
issues.title: Invalid Young-inequality lower bound in the impedance injectivity proof
issues.why_classification: The key uniqueness step fails and the source gives no alternative route; impedance well-posedness is lost without a new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Symmetry of e(u,v) requires (n^T Hu n, Δv) = (Δu, n^T Hv n), which needs identities like (u_xy,v_xx)=(u_xx,v_xy). These hold only when ∇u=∇v=0 on ∂Ω. The space H^2_0 is defined as H^2∩H^1_0, where ∂_νu need not vanish, so boundary terms remain and e is not symmetric in general. Regularity alone does not justify the swaps. The expansion is also wrong: Δ(n^T Hu n) has mixed coefficient n_x^2+n_y^2, not (n_x+n_y)^2, and the expression ∇·∇[n^T(n^T∇u)] is garbled.

failure_location.quote: Due to the regularity of the functions $u, v \in H^2_0(\Omega)$, we can swap the order of differentiation and integrate by parts to show that the last two terms in \eqref{eq:exp} are self-adjoint as well.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove symmetry with explicit boundary terms in the actual space, or work in the clamped space {u∈H^2: u=∂_νu=0} for the eigenproblem, and correct the expansion.
issues.overall_effect: The real-eigenvalue, orthogonal-basis and T-construction machinery for β>0 relies on symmetry that is unproven (and false) in the stated space.
issues.title: Self-adjointness proof for the nematic eigenproblem is incorrect on H^2∩H^1_0 and uses a wrong expansion
issues.why_classification: A contained change of space or an added boundary-term argument restores the claim, but it affects the sound-soft setup rather than a typo.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, it holds that $\Vert R_h \Vert_{\mathcal{L}(X,X)} \le (\Vert A \Vert_{\mathcal{L}(X,X)} \Vert T_h \Vert_{\mathcal{L}(X,X)}/\alpha_0)$

issues.failure_explanation: Uniform T_h-coercivity of A gives α0||w_h||^2 ≤ |(A w_h, T_h w_h)| with the same w_h in both slots. Applied to w_h=L_h v_h it yields T_h L_h v_h, not T_h v_h, so the displayed inequality is unjustified. The argument yields at most discrete inf-sup stability, not coercivity with the same T_h. The proof also needs sup_h||T_h||<∞, which is not a hypothesis of the theorem, and the density of X_h in X appears only in a footnote. The sesquilinear slot convention for T (Definition uses a(Tu,u), proof uses (Av,Tv)) is inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with the hypotheses it needs (uniform bound on T_h, density of X_h) and the conclusion the proof supports (uniform discrete inf-sup stability), then run the best-approximation argument with inf-sup.
issues.overall_effect: The asymptotic T_h-coercivity of the impedance operator 𝒜_h, on which the discrete well-posedness and best-approximation results for impedance conditions rest, is not established as stated.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem vBZThm does not give T_h-coercivity with the same T_h
issues.why_classification: The weaker inf-sup conclusion is enough for quasi-optimality, so the repair is a contained restatement and reproof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notice that we are assuming that $h$ is small enough such that $\lambda^{(i_{\ast})}_h < k^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: γ is a minimum over the discrete eigenvalues of C(λ_h)|λ_h-k^2|. Uniform positivity needs λ_h^(i*) to stay bounded away from k^2 from below and λ_h^(i*+1) from above, plus control of the renormalisation constants, as h→0. This requires convergence of the (Nitsche-)discrete eigenvalues to the continuous ones, which is never shown. Only λ_h^(i*)<k^2 is assumed. For ε=1 the form is nonconforming, so λ_h^(i*+1)>k^2 is not guaranteed either, and equivalence of the eigenfunction expansion norm with ||·||_ε is not argued.

issues.overall_effect: Uniform discrete T_h-coercivity, and hence h-independent quasi-optimality constants, are not established for either β=0 or β>0.
issues.title: Uniformity in h of the T_h-coercivity constant is asserted without discrete eigenvalue convergence or spectral gap
issues.why_classification: Standard discrete spectral convergence theory could fill the gap, but it is a new contained lemma, not a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: T-coercivity is defined as a(Tu,u) with T in the first (trial) argument. Galerkin orthogonality a_h(u-u_h,·)=0 holds only with the error in the first slot, so it applies to a_h(w,T_h w), not a_h(T_h w,w). The step a_h(T_h w,w) ≤ ||T_h|| a_h(u-v_h,w) is also not a valid inequality for a sesquilinear form. In the nonsymmetric impedance case a_h(T_h w,w)≠a_h(w,T_h w), so the argument is invalid as written.

issues.why_classification: In the symmetric sound-soft case the slots coincide; in general the repair is a short consistent reversal of the slot convention plus checking the earlier proofs.

issues.failure_explanation: The norm ||·||_{h,ε} contains only the unweighted term ε||u_h||^2_{L^2(∂Ω)}, while a_h contains the penalty η_1 h^{-3}(u_h,v_h)_{∂Ω}+η_2 h^{-1}(u_h,v_h)_{∂Ω}. These are not bounded by ||u_h||_{h,ε}||v_h||_{h,ε} with an h-independent constant (functions with O(1) boundary values break it). Coercivity, by contrast, is proved only in this weaker norm. Moreover ||·||_{h,ε} involves traces of ∇Δ(u-v_h) and is applied to u-v_h with u∈X, which is undefined for u∈H^2.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: then there exists $h_0 > 0$ such that $\mathcal{A}$ is uniformly $T_h$-coercive on $X_h$ for all $h \le h_0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims that checking λ_h^(i*)<k^2 yields all assumptions. For impedance conditions, stability of 𝒜_h additionally needs h≤h_0 from the compact-perturbation theorem, which is non-explicit and not checkable. Penalty parameters must also be large, and i* is defined through the continuous spectrum. The criterion alone does not guarantee the stated assumptions or quasi-optimality.
